summary: T2 meets the m1 requirements by static review of the diff. The platform layer uses a real clock, a bounded 5 ms spin sleep, an rAF-driven main loop, a canvas blit with a frame counter and a title hook. doom-boot.js sets the global Module before doom.js, builds args from the query string and always passes -iwad doom1.wad. All URLs are relative, build.sh packages the WAD with --preload-file and copies web/* into dist/doom. No test-only exports were added. I did not re-run the build, because the controller's m1 run already passed. Only minor robustness notes remain.

findings.criterion: No uncaught exceptions; surface fatal errors on the page
findings.evidence: web/doom-boot.js:36-50 only hooks Module.onExit and Module.onAbort; there is no window 'error' or 'unhandledrejection' listener
findings.summary: A JS exception thrown from inside the main loop, such as an I_Error that is not routed through exit, is not shown in the fatal banner. The risk is small.

findings.evidence: web/doom-boot.js:38-47 uses a synchronous XHR with a binary-string conversion for doom.data
findings.summary: This works but is deprecated on the main thread and slow for the shareware WAD (about 4 MB). The doom.data URL is relative, so subpath loading is not affected.
EnMm and a bare map number are handled. A MAPnn value is treated as a bare number, which is harmless for Episode 1.
